report.summary: Reviewed scheduler.py chunk 1: docstring claims parsed; several claims kept, some uncheckable, no broken claims found in this window.
risks: gate_concurrent_writes docstring | medium | Claims about TaskAttempt and gated_writes behavior cannot be verified from this chunk; need to inspect those modules. | Inspect daedalus/spine/attempt.py and daedalus/kairos/gated_writes.py
dispatch docstring | medium | Claims about offload() snapshot/rollback behavior and gated path details are uncheckable here; need offload.py. | Inspect daedalus/offload.py
accept docstring | medium | Claim about repo_root roster visibility cannot be verified; need route_and_select implementation. | Inspect provider_router.py
FREE_LANES and DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY | low | Constants are defined but not fully documented; behavior depends on route_and_select. | Inspect provider_router.py

handoff.purpose: Review docstring claims against implementation for the scheduler's accept/plan/dispatch/gate_concurrent_writes methods and constants.

symbols.name: FREE_LANES
symbols.note: Tuple of lane names dispatch may use; excludes claude_cli.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY
symbols.note: Default availability dict: claude_cli and ollama True, deepseek and codex_cli False.

symbols.name: _paths_overlap
symbols.note: Diagnostic overlap check among write-mode assignments' declared paths.

symbols.name: Assignment
symbols.note: Dataclass holding objective, paths, owner, lane, worker, mode, accepted, reason.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler
symbols.note: Scheduler dataclass with max_workers, availability, policy, project, active_agents, max_parallel_writes, _bench.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler.__post_init__
symbols.note: Initializes bench cycle and loads project policy/team config if project set.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler.accept
symbols.note: Routes tasks via route_and_select; bounces non-free-lane tasks; returns Assignment list.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler.plan
symbols.note: Calls accept; computes waves and returns dict with assignments, spawned, bounced, waves.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler.dispatch
symbols.note: Runs accepted tasks via offload; supports dry_run and parallel advisory-only; sequential for writes.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler._bounced_or_planned
symbols.note: Inner helper returning bounced or planned result dict; None if live run needed.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler._run_one
symbols.note: Inner helper invoking offload and returning result dict with wrote list.

symbols.name: KairosScheduler.gate_concurrent_writes
symbols.note: Docstring describes Phase 1 gating; body not present in this chunk.

claims.text: dynamically spawns local workers from a bounded pool (the Mexican/Italian Ollama bench; the Chinese DeepSeek bench stays dormant without a key)
claims.why: The module defines DEFAULT_AVAILABILITY with deepseek False and _bench cycles over roster('ollama'); __post_init__ sets the bench from ollama roster, so local pool is bounded and DeepSeek dormant by default.

claims.text: briefs each with a scoped task + the owning specialist's domain
claims.why: Assignment includes objective, paths, owner, lane, worker; accept() passes objective, paths, agent name, lane, persona, mode to Assignment.

claims.text: enforces their *reduced rights* (the Ollama write-guard already refuses device/vendor/secret/high-risk paths)
claims.why: The write-guard behavior is not implemented in this chunk; it is attributed to another component (Ollama write-guard).

claims.text: returns a consolidated report for Adam / the owning specialist to review
claims.why: dispatch() and plan() return dicts containing assignments, results, and per-task statuses; accept() returns Assignment list with owner fields.

claims.text: Kairos never talks to the user, never decides trust, and bounces anything that belongs to the senior crew back to the trusted orchestration layer.
claims.why: accept() bounces tasks whose provider is not in FREE_LANES with reason 'belongs to the senior crew -> return to Adam'; no user interaction code exists.

claims.text: This is not a proof of write isolation: an agent may touch an undeclared path.
claims.why: The function only checks declared paths; the docstring explicitly disclaims proof of isolation.

claims.text: Production write concurrency therefore remains disabled until each task owns a separate Forge workcell/worktree.
claims.why: dispatch() only allows parallel when no writes; writes remain sequential unless using gate_concurrent_writes, which is described as separate.

claims.text: Concurrency cap SPECIFICALLY for gate_concurrent_writes ... independent of max_workers.
claims.why: The field max_parallel_writes is defined separately from max_workers, and __post_init__ parses it independently.

claims.text: every concurrent write-mode offload() triggers a FULL structcore re-index ... NOT MEASURED on this box for N>1
claims.why: The re-index behavior is described as coming from offload.py and structcore; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: repo_root makes the target repo's own .agentenv/agents/ roster visible to routing (without it only global agents route)
claims.why: The routing logic is in route_and_select; this chunk only passes repo_root through.

claims.text: Dry run: who gets spawned, in how many bounded waves.
claims.why: plan() computes waves and returns spawned count; it does not actually spawn.

claims.text: dry_run stops at the spawn plan; live actually invokes each bench worker through the provider seam.
claims.why: In dispatch, if dry_run, _bounced_or_planned returns status 'planned' and _run_one is not called; if not dry_run, _run_one calls offload with live=True.

claims.text: Sequential by default (parallel=False): each live write is verified by diffing a WHOLE-repo content-hash snapshot around that one run (offload._repo_snapshot), which catches even writes outside --paths -- but two such runs on one repo concurrently would cross-attribute disk_changed.
claims.why: The snapshot behavior is in offload._repo_snapshot; not visible here.

claims.text: parallel=True currently overlaps advisory-only work.
claims.why: can_parallel = parallel and not has_writes; has_writes is true if any write-mode task exists.

claims.text: Declared path disjointness is not a security boundary: a writable agent can touch an undeclared repository path, while isolate_paths=True would observe only its hints and misattribute the result.
claims.why: The behavior of isolate_paths is not implemented in this chunk; it is passed to offload.

claims.text: Writable concurrency stays sequential with whole-repository snapshots until Forge gives every attempt its own workcell/worktree.
claims.why: In dispatch, writes are not parallelized; can_parallel requires not has_writes.

claims.text: the isolation now EXISTS -- see gate_concurrent_writes() below, which runs each write through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt (its own worktree, its own hardened patch capture) fanned out concurrently, and daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.promote_candidates(), which lands gated candidates one at a time behind a cross-process lock with cumulative re-gating.
claims.why: This references other modules and methods not present in this chunk; the gate_concurrent_writes body is not shown.

claims.text: What THAT path returns is not what this one returns, though: a gated PatchArtifact the primary checkout never saw, not a live write already sitting in repo_root's working tree.
claims.why: This describes behavior of gate_concurrent_writes and gated_writes; not visible here.

claims.text: dispatch() keeps its existing auto-land contract for a single write (offload() has always auto-landed a sequential one)
claims.why: offload()'s behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Call gate_concurrent_writes()/promote_candidates() explicitly when that decision says to.
claims.why: The comment instructs explicit calls; the dispatch code does not call them, consistent with the instruction.

claims.text: Safe concurrent WRITE dispatch: PHASE 1 only (gating, not landing).
claims.why: The method body is not present in this chunk; cannot verify behavior.

claims.text: Every write task in tasks runs CONCURRENTLY, each through daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt in its own worktree (offload() as the runner -- its verify+rollback cascade stays the authority for per-task correctness; see daedalus.kairos.gated_writes._relay_gate).
claims.why: References other modules and method body not present.

claims.text: Returns one daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.GatedCandidate per accepted write task: a gate verdict plus a PatchArtifact when clean.
claims.why: Return type not visible; method body absent.

claims.text: The primary checkout at repo_root is NEVER touched by this call -- that is TaskAttempt's own structural guarantee (see tests/test_spine_attempt.py::test_happy_path_artifact_and_primary_untouched).
claims.why: References external test and TaskAttempt; not verifiable here.

claims.text: Advisory-only tasks are bounced (this method only accepts write-mode work; use plan()/accept() for the routing verdict on the rest of a mixed task list, or dispatch() to actually run them).
claims.why: Method body not present; cannot verify bounce behavior.

claims.text: cancel, when given, is forwarded unchanged to ...
claims.why: The sentence is truncated; the rest of the claim is not visible.

observations.what: gate_concurrent_writes method body is absent from this chunk; its docstring makes many strong claims about behavior in other modules.
dispatch() uses ThreadPoolExecutor for advisory-only parallel runs, but the max_workers default is 3, which is a low bound.
The _bench cycle is initialized from roster('ollama') but never used in this chunk; it may be used elsewhere or unused.
